abstract:
We give a quantum algorithm for evaluating formulas over an extended gate set, including all twoand three-bit binary gates (e.g., NAND, 3-majority). The algorithm is optimal on read-once formulas for which each gate's inputs are balanced in a certain sense.

The main new tool is a correspondence between a classical linear-algebraic model of computation, "span programs," and weighted bipartite graphs. A span program's evaluation corresponds to an eigenvalue-zero eigenvector of the associated graph. A quantum computer can therefore evaluate the span program by applying spectral estimation to the graph.

For example, the classical complexity of evaluating the balanced ternary majority formula is unknown, and the natural generalization of randomized alpha-beta pruning is known to be suboptimal. In contrast, our algorithm generalizes the optimal quantum AND-OR formula evaluation algorithm and is optimal for evaluating the balanced ternary majority formula.

specification.problem: Evaluate formulas over an extended gate set (all 2- and 3-bit binary gates, e.g. NAND, 3-majority) with a quantum algorithm, by mapping span programs to weighted bipartite graphs so that span program evaluation corresponds to an eigenvalue-zero eigenvector of the graph, and applying spectral estimation.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction of the span-program-to-graph correspondence and the spectral-estimation evaluation idea; circuit details, weights, and complexity proofs are not reconstructed.

symbols.meaning: span program computing a Boolean function
weighted bipartite graph associated with P
input bit string to the formula
weighted adjacency operator of the graph

equations.label: Span program evaluation as zero eigenvector
equations.latex: f(x)=1 \iff A_{G_P(x)}\,|\psi\rangle=0 \text{ for some nonzero } |\psi\rangle \text{ supported near the output vertex}
equations.description: Schematic statement that evaluation corresponds to an eigenvalue-zero eigenvector of the graph; the exact support condition is an assumption.
equations.abstract_quote: A span program's evaluation corresponds to an eigenvalue-zero eigenvector of the associated graph.
equations.justification: Schematic formalization of the abstract sentence; precise condition not given.
assumptions: Support condition and the 0/1 direction convention are assumed

equations.label: Spectral estimation
equations.latex: U=e^{iA_G t},\quad \text{phase estimation of } U \text{ distinguishes eigenvalue } 0 \text{ from gap } \ge \Delta
equations.description: Spectral estimation applied to the graph operator via phase estimation of a unitary built from it.
equations.justification: Standard way to realize spectral estimation; the abstract only names it.
assumptions: Spectral gap Delta around zero in the relevant case

registers.name: vertex
registers.role: Position register: basis states are graph vertices, the space on which A_G acts

registers.name: phase
registers.role: Ancilla register holding the phase estimation output for the eigenvalue of A_G

specification.initial_state: Vertex register in the basis state of a designated input/output vertex of G_P(x); phase register in |0>^m.

steps.description: Build the graph G_P(x) from the span program and input x, with oracle queries to x determining which edges are present.
Prepare the vertex register at the designated vertex and apply Hadamards to the phase register.
Apply controlled powers of U=e^{iA_G t} (implemented by a Hamiltonian simulation or walk) from the phase register onto the vertex register, then the inverse QFT.

specification.measurement: Measure the phase register in the computational basis. Outcome 0 (eigenvalue within the estimation precision of zero) indicates the zero-eigenvector overlap, i.e. f(x)=1 under the assumed convention; a nonzero outcome indicates f(x)=0.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Repeat the run a constant number of times and take a majority vote on whether the phase outcome is within the threshold of zero. Threshold and precision are assumed to be of order Delta; output the Boolean f(x) accordingly.
assumptions: Equations are schematic, not the paper's exact construction
Phase estimation is used as the spectral estimation method
Initial vertex and register sizes are assumed, not given in the abstract
Initial state is the designated input vertex of the graph; register sizes are symbolic
Measurement is a phase-register readout with a zero-vs-nonzero threshold, and the 0/1 convention is assumed
missing_information: Success threshold and precision are not specified in the abstract
Exact initial state and Hamiltonian simulation implementation are not stated in the abstract
Paper's actual measurement and postprocessing are not given in the abstract
